title: Calculus with Parametric and Polar Curves

questions.q: Given $x(t) = t^3 - 3t$ and $y(t) = t^2 + 1$, find $\frac{dy}{dx}$ in terms of $t$.
Find the equation of the tangent line to the parametric curve $x = 2\cos t, y = 3\sin t$ at $t = \pi/4$.
questions.answer: At $t = \pi/4$: $x = \sqrt{2}, y = 3\sqrt{2}/2$. $dx/dt = -2\sin t = -\sqrt{2}$; $dy/dt = 3\cos t = 3\sqrt{2}/2$. Slope $\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{3\sqrt{2}/2}{-\sqrt{2}} = -\frac{3}{2}$. Line: $y - \frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2} = -\frac{3}{2}(x - \sqrt{2})$.

sections.heading: Section 3: Slopes and Tangents of Polar Curves

questions.q: Given $r = f(\theta)$, how are the Cartesian coordinates related to polar coordinates?
questions.answer: The standard polar to Cartesian conversion is $x = r\cos\theta = f(\theta)\cos\theta$ and $y = r\sin\theta = f(\theta)\sin\theta$.

questions.q: Find the slope $\frac{dy}{dx}$ of the polar curve $r = 2$ at $\theta = \pi/4$.
questions.answer: Since $r = 2$ is a circle centered at the origin, the radius vector at $\theta = \pi/4$ has slope $\tan(\pi/4) = 1$. The tangent line is perpendicular to the radial line, so its slope is $-1$.

questions.q: At what angles $\theta \in [0, \pi)$ does the cardioid $r = 1 + \cos\theta$ pass through the pole ($r = 0$)?
State the formula for the area enclosed by a polar curve $r = f(\theta)$ from $\theta = \alpha$ to $\theta = \beta$.
questions.answer: An infinitesimal sector with central angle $d\theta$ has area $dA = \frac{1}{2}r^2 d\theta$, giving $A = \frac{1}{2}\int_\alpha^\beta r^2\,d\theta$.

questions.q: Find the area enclosed by one petal of the four-petaled rose $r = 2\cos(2\theta)$.
